input.prompt:
3D highly rendered animation, soft 3D CGI look. Exactly four characters: Barnaby, Hazel, Anne and Baba. Only one Barnaby is in the frame. Subtitle-free, no logo, no watermark.

REFERENCES: @Image 1 gives Barnaby's head, antlers and colours and @Image 7 gives his full body in profile facing right; @Image 2 gives Hazel; @Image 3 gives Baba and @Image 4 gives Anne, both full body; @Image 5 is the brass bell on its pole; @Image 6 is the location. Every Barnaby reference gives identity only, never size or crop: Barnaby stays at about 45 to 55 percent of the frame height, full antlers inside the frame with clear headroom.

CHARACTERS: Barnaby: chubby moose upright on his two hind legs like a person, red knit sweater with ribbed cuffs; antlers dark chocolate-brown, slightly darker than his fur, about 1.8 times his head width, short round prongs; giant round matte anthracite nose about half as wide as his face, short thick caramel-brown muzzle ending right behind the nose, big round amber-copper eyes, thick brown brows. Hazel: tiny chibi chipmunk, round head about 45 percent of her body, one dark chocolate forehead stripe, flat mint scarf, bushy S-curved tail that stays a big bushy S-curve the whole time, plump cream cheeks, two very big glossy solid black eyes. Baba: large moose father upright like a person, dark chestnut fur with grey grizzle, thick dark brows, half-closed eyelids over amber eyes, grey beard, round gold-rimmed glasses, plain forest-green knit sweater with a round ribbed collar; symmetric dark chocolate velvet antlers about 2.1 times his head width, four short thick round-tipped prongs per side; blunt face-coloured muzzle, giant round matte anthracite nose. Anne: moose mother upright like a person, no antlers, smooth round head, big round ears, dark chocolate-brown fur with a cream belly, amber irises, thick mustard-yellow knit shawl without fringe tied at her chest; blunt face-coloured muzzle, giant round matte anthracite nose. FORBIDDEN: any tail, tuft or tail-like bump on Barnaby; a small or shiny nose on Barnaby; Baba's antlers on Barnaby; white eye-whites on Hazel; antlers or buds on Anne; a patterned sweater on Baba; human fingers on any character; a second Barnaby; a fifth character.

LIGHT: silver full moon gives a thin cool rim light from the upper back; four paper lanterns give one soft, even, constant golden light that warms the faces. Barnaby's fur stays warm caramel-brown and his sweater deep red, Baba's sweater forest green, Anne's shawl mustard-yellow; the night is deep blue, never black.

SUBJECT & ACTION: Barnaby stands at the far left of the picture at the edge of the lantern light, facing the picture-right, Hazel on his shoulder on the left side of the picture with one small smooth capless hazelnut clasped to her chest. A red maple leaf is already stuck to the red sleeve of his near arm with an amber syrup smear, already there from the very first moment; it stays in the same place for the whole clip. Anne stands in front of the table to the left of the middle of the picture, about a body and a half to the right of Barnaby, her face turned away to the dark meadow on the left, ears forward. Baba stands in front of the table at its right end by the bell pole, his forehoof resting against the short braided cord, his eyes on the meadow. Nobody sits at the table.
Seconds 0 to 1.5: Barnaby takes two small soft steps to the right in the dry leaves into the edge of the golden light, his eyes on Anne; one dry leaf crunches under his hind hoof at about second 0.9 and Anne's ears swivel toward the sound.
At second 1.5 Anne turns her head and shoulders toward Barnaby, to the left of the picture, her ears forward, her head tilted a little to one side, her eyes locked on his face, and says curiously and softly, her lips moving to the words, 'Who's there?' while she stays where she is, leaning slightly forward. Barnaby stops and stands still, his eyes wide on Anne, his ears up.
At about second 3.0 Hazel leans her head against Barnaby's cheek, her eyes on the brass bell, and whispers, her lips moving to the words, 'They kept the bell for you.'
At about second 4.5 Barnaby's eyes go to the brass bell and he whispers, his lips moving to the words, 'They waited...' His brows lift at the inner ends, his eyes glisten, his ears tip forward and one small soft smile appears; he breathes out once. At second 5.0 Baba's eyes slide to Barnaby, his brows rising, his hoof staying on the cord. Barnaby's antlers stay on his head the whole time. He keeps his back straight and tall and never drops onto four legs.

SCENE: four round white paper lanterns hang still on one twine rope above the table, from the top of the tall wooden bell pole on the right to the maples on the left; a long wooden table with a golden pie, a bowl of cranberries, two corn cobs and a loaf of bread, nobody sitting, no chairs, benches or stools; a brass bell on a bracket on the bell pole at the right end of the table with one short braided cord hanging straight down, already there from the very first moment; a moonlit meadow of red and burgundy maples and fallen red leaves, a deep blue sky, no snow.

CAMERA: a steady medium wide shot of all four, Barnaby about 45 percent of the frame height, single continuous take from second 0 to 6.0, no cut. One slow smooth push-in from second 1.5 to second 5.0, then the camera holds: Barnaby grows from about 45 to at most 55 percent of the frame height and stays there; Baba and the bell pole stay inside the frame on the right. Barnaby's full antlers stay inside the frame with clear headroom above them the whole shot (and every other character's antlers too), at least 25 percent of the frame height above the tallest antlers.

SOUND: only natural on-set sounds: a dry night breeze, soft hoof steps in dry leaves at the start with one crisp leaf crunch at about second 0.9, a faint fabric rustle, each word heard once, Barnaby warm young male voice, Hazel tiny bright girl voice, Anne warm motherly voice, Baba warm low father voice, one line at a time.
